item.text: {"overall_decision":"manual_review","chapters":[{"chapter_id":"1B","decision":"pass","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0007","reason":"Humanitarian grain-corridor mediation is relevant to de-escalation, but it is not direct nuclear or existential-risk decision evidence and should stay contextual rather than decisive."},{"evidence_id":"E0008","reason":"The Istanbul coordination-centre evidence supports broader diplomacy, but it is food-security logistics rather than a nuclear-risk choice."},{"evidence_id":"E0009","reason":"The Finland/Sweden NATO memorandum is alliance bargaining, not direct evidence of nuclear command, safety, or doctrine choices."},{"evidence_id":"E0010","reason":"This quotation is useful for attributing bargaining posture, but it is still general security diplomacy rather than nuclear-risk conduct."},{"evidence_id":"E0011","reason":"The Syria/Iraq airstrikes are conventional force-use evidence; their relevance to 1B is only indirect escalation-risk context."},{"evidence_id":"E0012","reason":"The threatened land operation is a conventional escalation signal, not a direct nuclear or existential-risk act."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Direct 2022 nuclear-specific conduct is sparse; most positive evidence is alliance or humanitarian diplomacy rather than nuclear command, doctrine, or safety reform.","lenses":["1B.2","1B.3","1B.7","1B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"NATO/IAEA/CTBTO records plus Turkish-language reporting on any 2022 nuclear-safety, custody, or doctrine decisions.","why_it_matters":"Without direct nuclear-risk choices, the chapter depends on limited-exposure inference rather than ruler-specific nuclear conduct."},{"gap":"The package shows limited exposure and inherited NATO structure, but not a strong ruler-attributed improvement or deterioration in nuclear posture.","lenses":["1B.4","1B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Official treaty/consultation records and contemporaneous Turkish presidential or defense statements on nuclear policy.","why_it_matters":"This affects whether the chapter is a fair limited-exposure case or merely a structural context note."}],"reason":"The package is usable as a limited-exposure case and does distinguish inherited alliance posture, indirect de-escalation, and conventional escalation. It just needs those non-nuclear items kept in context rather than treated as decisive 1B evidence."},{"chapter_id":"2B","decision":"pass","remove_or_contextualize":[],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"The package is strong on mediation and selective coercion, but weaker on independent verification of the civilian-harm allegations and on Erdoğan's own weighing of peaceful alternatives for the Syria/Iraq operations.","lenses":["2B.2","2B.4","2B.6","2B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Independent investigations, UN/ICRC material, and Turkish-language contemporaneous reporting on operational authorization and civilian impact.","why_it_matters":"This is the main remaining uncertainty on proportionality, civilian protection, and ruler attribution."}],"reason":"The chapter fairly presents both peace-brokering and coercive conduct, with explicit contrary evidence and attribution caveats. The package is mixed but adequate."},{"chapter_id":"3B","decision":"pass","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0032","reason":"Press-freedom detention is primarily 4B/7B repression evidence; it only indirectly bears on domestic physical safety."},{"evidence_id":"E0033","reason":"This is a civic-space and detention item that belongs mainly in 4B/7B, not as core 3B physical-integrity evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0034","reason":"The Imamoglu sentencing is opposition suppression and political-fear evidence; it is secondary to 4B rather than a central 3B safety item."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Several items are civic-space or press-repression evidence rather than direct physical-integrity harm, so the chapter partly relies on fear-climate inference.","lenses":["3B.5","3B.8","3B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Domestic-violence enforcement records, custody-abuse monitoring, and independent reporting on police/prosecutorial conduct in 2022.","why_it_matters":"It affects whether the evidence is directly about domestic safety or is partly imported from adjacent chapters."},{"gap":"Attribution for some harms is institutional rather than command-specific, especially for local policing and court actions.","lenses":["3B.2","3B.4"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"High-level directives, ministerial oversight records, and independent findings on police and prosecutorial accountability.","why_it_matters":"This determines how much can fairly be pinned on Erdoğan rather than on lower-level actors."}],"reason":"The package fairly covers recurring domestic-violence failures, protest policing, and hostile rhetoric, while preserving contrary evidence and reform steps. The main issue is cross-chapter contamination, not absence of a usable 3B record."},{"chapter_id":"4B","decision":"pass","remove_or_contextualize":[],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"There was no true 2022 succession or term-limit stress test, so the chapter relies on institutional erosion and media/election-law evidence instead of a direct transfer-of-power event.","lenses":["4B.8","4B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Constitutional and election-law records plus contemporaneous analysis of the April 2022 electoral changes and judicial enforcement.","why_it_matters":"It limits how much the package can say about transfer norms in 2022 specifically."}],"reason":"The package is strong and internally coherent on institutional capture, media control, electoral-law changes, and opposition pressure, with appropriate contrary evidence and attribution limits."},{"chapter_id":"5B","decision":"pass","remove_or_contextualize":[],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Outcomes are heavily confounded by inflation shocks, external demand, the post-pandemic rebound, and CBRT formal independence, so causal credit remains partial.","lenses":["5B.3","5B.9","5B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"IMF/World Bank/OECD staff work that disentangles policy, external shocks, and household effects in 2022.","why_it_matters":"This is the main limit on attributing macro outcomes directly to Erdoğan."},{"gap":"Project-level delivery and regional/household distribution evidence are thinner than macro indicators.","lenses":["5B.6","5B.8"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Budget execution, procurement audits, and household or regional welfare series tied to 2022 programs.","why_it_matters":"It constrains how confidently the package can move from macro outcomes to ruler competence."}],"reason":"The chapter presents a plausible 2022 economic record with both adverse macro evidence and some targeted relief, while separating plans, implementation, and outcomes."},{"chapter_id":"6B","decision":"pass","remove_or_contextualize":[],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"The strongest welfare evidence is on health coverage and refugee cash transfers; housing, sanitation, and school-quality evidence is thinner.","lenses":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.4"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"WHO/UNICEF/education-sector evaluations and Turkish budget or delivery data for 2022.","why_it_matters":"This limits breadth across the welfare portfolio."},{"gap":"Several positive items are donor-UNICEF/WHO partnerships, so Erdoğan attribution is meaningful but not exclusive.","lenses":["6B.4","6B.9","6B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Government budget execution and line-ministry delivery records for the relevant programs.","why_it_matters":"It affects how much of the welfare record can be credited to Erdoğan versus inherited or externally supported systems."}],"reason":"The package fairly presents broad welfare gains alongside persistent inequality, refugee pressure, and macro harm. It is balanced, cited, and explicit about shared attribution."},{"chapter_id":"7B","decision":"manual_review","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0077","reason":"This is allegation-level family-network material; Reuters could not confirm Erdoğan or Bilal Erdoğan's awareness or involvement, so it should not be treated as direct personal-corruption proof."},{"evidence_id":"E0078","reason":"The son-in-law lawsuit is family-network litigation, not direct evidence of Erdoğan's own dishonesty, self-enrichment, or hidden conflicts."},{"evidence_id":"E0079","reason":"This is another family-linked complaint about reporting; it is relevant context, but not direct proof of Erdoğan's personal integrity failures."},{"evidence_id":"E0096","reason":"The 2023 Reuters complaint remains unproven and explicitly lacks confirmation of Erdoğan's involvement, so it is context only for 2022."},{"evidence_id":"E0097","reason":"The asset declaration is out of period for 2022 and cannot resolve the 2022 personal-integrity question."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"There is no direct 2022 audited asset, gift, or procurement record for Erdoğan personally.","lenses":["7B.3","7B.4"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Official asset declarations, audited financial disclosures, procurement records, or court/inquiry findings from 2022.","why_it_matters":"Without a personal financial record, the chapter leans too much on inference and family-network proximity."},{"gap":"The strongest negative items are media-control and family-network allegations, not direct first-person dishonesty or self-dealing proof.","lenses":["7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Primary legal findings or direct documentary evidence of Erdoğan's own statements, corrections, or benefit from the contested conduct.","why_it_matters":"This is the main reason the chapter is not ready for clean publication."}],"reason":"This is the only chapter where the package still depends heavily on allegation-level family-network material and institutional media pressure rather than direct, ruler-specific integrity evidence. It is reviewable, but not clean enough to pass without further adjudication."},{"chapter_id":"8B","decision":"pass","remove_or_contextualize":[],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Project-level completion evidence is thin; the package shows allocation, program design, and some outcomes, but not audited delivery for specific 2022 initiatives.","lenses":["8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Execution audits, ministry completion reports, and independent evaluations of major 2022 investments and macro measures.","why_it_matters":"It limits confidence in implementation claims even where the program direction is clear."},{"gap":"Outcome attribution is still confounded by shocks and by private-sector behavior, especially on growth, exports, and labor-market statistics.","lenses":["8B.7","8B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"IMF/OECD/World Bank causal analysis and project-specific implementation tracking for 2022.","why_it_matters":"It affects how strongly the observed outcomes can be credited to Erdoğan's competence rather than context."}],"reason":"The package is coherent on program, mobilization, execution signals, and end-of-year outcomes. It is also appropriately cautious about attribution and confounding."}]}
